title: Hobeika 2020 · Audience
citation: Hobeika, Taffou, and Viaud-Delmon (2020). Social impact on audiotactile integration near the body. Acoustical Science and Technology, 41(1), 345–348.
notes: The software assessment runs one response stream over 480 trials. The operator seats a passive partner during the audience blocks and leaves the chair empty during the isolated blocks. The trial budget and silent-window timing use the matched procedure in the author's thesis.

published_method.relationship: The parallel Royal Society Open Science report has the same three assessments, analyzed counts and multiple statistics. Participant-level overlap is unverified.
published_method.audio: Three-second binaural bubbling water at −60° or +60°, approaching from 135 to 20 cm in an IRCAM Spat room simulation with LISTEN HRTFs.
published_method.sound_gaps: Original waveform, renderer patch and calibration are unavailable.
published_method.tactile: 20 ms, 250 Hz sinusoid delivered by a 28 mm miniature loudspeaker to palmar left index.
published_method.baselines: Periods nominally −650 and +3650 ms relative to sound onset, using actual silent windows around sound in the thesis procedure.
published_method.posture: Seated in a fixed side position, hands covered, partner at 100 cm in dyad compared with isolated condition.
published_method.response: Speeded right-finger response to touch, withhold on audio-only. Analyze effects by sound side and social context.
published_method.dyad_instruction: The seated partner is inactive and both participants are told that the task is individual.

stimulus_type.value: Bubbling-water sound plus palmar index vibration

remaining_caveats: The toolkit uses generated pink noise and its binaural engine. Original bubbling-water audio, LISTEN filters, room response and calibrated headphone output are still needed for source-equivalent delivery.

The preview generates the reported 250 Hz, 20 ms waveform at a digital default and uses a mouse response. Calibrate the physical miniature loudspeaker and validate the button timing. Follow the paper's fixation and seating procedure.

The author's thesis supplies the trial allocation. The toolkit uses two balanced silence durations at the reported 2,700 and 3,300 ms endpoints. Original jitter draws, catch split and realized order are unreported.
reference_parameters.preview_scope: Two counterbalanced sets of five blocks. The active participant responds to touch while the passive partner remains still. All baseline trials keep their sound and place touch outside that sound window.
